transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with our daily transition huddle. We have a patient who's medically stable and has asked to go home under our hospital-at-home program if we can put together a safe plan. I understand the patient lives alone, so we'll need to make sure we've addressed the overnight caregiver requirement through remote monitoring and morning phone checks. Before I can sign off on the transition, I need to hear from each of you on your respective pieces — respiratory therapy on the oxygen order, utilization review on payer approval, social work on the caregiver agreement, and pharmacy on medication pack duration and the teaching appointment. Let's go around the room. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I can speak to the pharmacy piece. The discharge medication changes include a new insulin pen that requires one supervised teaching dose before the first home dose. I've prepared exactly a seven-day labeled medication pack, and I can provide the supervised insulin teaching at 17:00 tomorrow.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I can speak to the caregiver agreement. The patient's neighbor, Malik, has signed the program's required caregiver agreement. I have the signed agreement in my case-management folder. Malik will be physically present from 16:00 through 22:00 tomorrow, with a backup phone check at 08:00 the next morning. Since the patient lives alone, this arrangement — combined with remote vital-sign monitoring and the morning phone check — should satisfy the overnight caregiver requirement under our policy.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I can speak to the respiratory therapy piece. During today's walk test, the patient desaturated with exertion and now requires continuous oxygen at exactly 2 L/min. I've confirmed that a portable concentrator and stationary backup can be delivered to the apartment by exactly 15:00 tomorrow, which would allow a hospital-at-home start at 16:00. I'll document the oxygen order at 2 L/min continuous in the transition record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I can speak to the utilization review piece. I've verified the patient's payer approval for hospital-at-home in the payer portal, and I have the approval reference on file. However, there's a specific condition attached to this approval that we need to account for in our planning: the first skilled-nurse visit must begin within four hours of the patient's arrival home, and remote vital-sign monitoring must be activated on the admission day. So when we're setting the hospital-at-home start time tomorrow, we'll need to make sure the skilled-nurse visit is scheduled within that four-hour window from arrival home.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thanks, everyone. From my side, I want to clarify the timing implications of the insulin teaching appointment. I've documented a seven-day medication pack and scheduled the supervised insulin teaching for 17:00 tomorrow. I understand from our policy that the teaching appointment can occur after admission, so it shouldn't be the factor that determines our hospital-at-home start time. The start time should be driven by equipment delivery and clinical readiness. Luis mentioned equipment can be delivered by 15:00, which could support a 16:00 start. My teaching at 17:00 would fall after that admission time, which is fine per our policy. Dr. Shah, from pharmacy's perspective, the medication pack duration and teaching appointment are both set and ready for your sign-off.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: Thanks, Evan. To clarify on the utilization review side: I've confirmed the payer approval is in place with the reference on file, and the two conditions I mentioned — the first skilled-nurse visit within four hours of arrival home and remote vital-sign monitoring activated on admission day — are both required under that approval. As Evan and Luis noted, if equipment delivery is feasible by 15:00 and we target a 16:00 admission, we'll just need to make sure a skilled-nurse visit is scheduled to begin by 20:00 at the latest and that remote monitoring is activated on the admission day. The standard admission process already schedules the first skilled-nurse visit within the payer's allowed window, so that should align. From my perspective, the payer approval reference is ready to be documented in the transition record for Dr. Shah's sign-off.
